title: Prefix Sums: Answer Range-Sum Queries in O(1)
oneLiner: Precompute running totals once, and any "sum of elements from i to j" becomes a single subtraction instead of a fresh loop.
keyTakeaway: A prefix sum array where prefix[i] = sum of the first i elements turns any range sum [i..j] into prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] -- O(1) per query after an O(n) one-time setup, instead of O(n) EVERY query if you re-sum the range from scratch each time.
explanation:
If a problem asks for the sum of elements between two indices MANY times (not just once), re-looping over the range from scratch every single query costs O(n) per query -- fine once, expensive across many queries on a big array. A PREFIX SUM array fixes this: prefix[0] = 0, and prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + nums[i-1] for i from 1 to n -- each entry is the running total of everything before it. Once built (a single O(n) pass), the sum of any range [i, j] (inclusive) is just prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] -- one subtraction, regardless of how wide the range is.

This works because prefix[j+1] already contains "everything up to and including j," and prefix[i] contains "everything up to but not including i" -- subtracting the second from the first cancels out everything before index i, leaving exactly the range [i, j]. Building this once and answering every query off it turns "M queries over an array of size N" from O(N*M) into O(N + M) -- the entire point when M is large.

visualizationSteps.message: prefix[0] = 0 -- the sum of nothing before index 0.
Query sum(nums[1..4]) = prefix[5] - prefix[1] = 14 - 3 = 11. One subtraction, no rescanning.

recognitionSignals: The problem asks for the sum (or average) of a RANGE/SUBARRAY, and especially if it asks for MANY such ranges.
You're about to write a loop inside a loop to sum a range for every query -- that's the O(N*M) shape prefix sums exist to avoid.
gotchas: Off-by-one is the constant danger: prefix has N+1 entries (prefix[0] = 0), and the range [left, right] inclusive is prefix[right+1] - prefix[left], not prefix[right] - prefix[left].
Rebuilding the prefix array for every query defeats the entire point -- build it ONCE, answer every query off the same array.
confusableWith: Sliding Window (this track) also processes a range of an array, but recomputes a WINDOW incrementally as it slides one element at a time; prefix sums answer a fixed, already-known range in one lookup with no incremental step needed.

complexity.note: O(n) to build the prefix array once; after that each range query is a single O(1) subtraction. Total for q queries: O(n + q).
